title: Before the city: the 1850s
caption: After the approach of Bruce Macdonald, Vancouver: A Visual History, 1992. Original drawing from cited sources.
note: Locations are approximate and shown at a general scale only. Names are spelled as the Nations publish them. Only sites with a published source are shown; many more places existed (Musqueam alone records 120+ place names), so blank areas are not empty land.

sites.name: X̱wáy̓x̱way
sites.use: Winter village; a large shell midden.
facts: Squamish people lived here for over 3,000 years; a longhouse over 60 m long housed about 100 people (Squamish Atlas).
The shell midden was about 8 ft deep and "acres in extent"; it was used to surface the first park road in 1888 (Matthews, Early Vancouver, vol. 4).
Families were pushed out by road building in the 1880s; one family stayed until 1923 (Squamish Atlas).
src: Matthews, Early Vancouver vol. 4 (City of Vancouver Archives)

sites.name: Sen̓áḵw
sites.en: Vanier Park, south end of Burrard Bridge
sites.use: Seasonal fishing, then a permanent village from about 1860. The Nation describes elk in the forests, cranberries in the marshes, and sturgeon and seal along the coast.
facts: One of 23 ancestral Squamish villages (Squamish Nation).
In 1913 families were forcibly removed and put on a barge (Squamish Nation; senakw.com). CBC reports about 20 families, roughly 150 people.
In 2003 the courts returned 10.48 acres of the original 80-acre reserve (Squamish Nation).
sites.short: Fishing; village from c. 1860; elk, cranberries, sturgeon, seal

sites.name: Iy̓ál̓mexw / ʔəy̓alməxʷ
sites.nation: Named by both Sḵwx̱wú7mesh (Iy̓ál̓mexw) and xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (ʔəy̓alməxʷ)
facts: The Squamish Atlas records summer fishing at Iy̓ál̓mexw.
The Musqueam Teaching Kit (Museum of Anthropology) names ʔəy̓alməxʷ as "Jericho Village".

sites.name: c̓əsnaʔəm
sites.en: Marpole, by the Fraser's North Arm
sites.use: A major village at the river mouth.
facts: First occupied almost 5,000 years ago (MOA); the City dates it to "at least 4,000 years".
One of the largest villages about 2,000–2,500 years ago (MOA, Musqueam). About 1,500 years ago people moved to xʷməθkʷəy̓əm (Musqueam).
Designated a National Historic Site in 1933 as the Marpole Midden. Part of the site at 8902 Milton Street has been returned to Musqueam.
src: MOA: c̓əsnaʔəm, the city before the city
sites.short: Major village, first occupied 4,000–5,000 years ago

sites.name: xʷməθkʷəy̓əm
sites.en: Musqueam, at the mouth of the Fraser's North Arm
sites.use: The main winter village at the river mouth.
facts: The Musqueam Teaching Kit says the main winter village was always at the mouth of the Fraser.
Today the main community is on Musqueam IR No. 2 (Government of Canada agreement text).
sites.short: Main winter village at the river mouth

sites.name: təmtəmíxʷtən
sites.use: Chum salmon fishery for about 2,500 years.
facts: The earliest levels date to about 1550 BCE (PLOS One, 2023).
Salmon bones show a chum fishery from about 850 BCE to 1650 CE (UBC, 2023).
sites.short: Chum salmon fishery, c. 850 BCE–1650 CE
